title: New Hires in Opinion

body_markdown:
Jasmine Sun, a leading voice on A.I., joins the team as a writer, and Alexa Sonnenfeld is the new chief of staff. Read more below from Opinion editor, Kathleen Kingsbury.


I’m delighted to tell you about two hires I’ve been eager to bring aboard: Jasmine Sun as Opinion’s newest writer and Alexa Sonnenfeld as our new chief of staff.


Photo Credit: Eugene Wei


**Jasmine Sun** has become one of the must-read voices on artificial intelligence, and now she’s writing for us. She’ll helm a weekly newsletter on A.I., help shape our editorials on technology and beyond, and appear on the relaunched “Hard Fork” podcast as an occasional guest and across our Opinion Shows.


If you’ve read her Substack or her April guest essay for us, “


[Silicon Valley Is Bracing for a Permanent Underclass](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/30/opinion/ai-labor-work-force-silicon-valley.html) ,” or


[heard her on Ezra Klein’s podcast](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/04/opinion/ezra-klein-podcast-jasmine-sun.html) in August, you already know what she brings. She’s a sharp, nuanced thinker who makes A.I. legible to experts and newcomers alike. She was tracking the backlash against data centers long before it became a story in the midterms.


She also knows Silicon Valley from the inside. As a product manager at Substack, she helped plan the strategies behind the platform’s growth. She co-founded Reboot, a publication for young technologists, and helped research and edit Kevin Roose’s latest book, “The A.G.I. Chronicles.”


Jasmine grew up in the Seattle area and has since become a devoted San Francisco evangelist. Ask her about a bakery, a trail or a weekend plan, and she’ll have an answer ready.


Photo Credit: Eugene Wei


Photo Credit: Johanna Matt-Navarro


Alexa Sonnenfeld joins us as chief of staff. She’s new to The Times but not to the pace and nuance of the job. As chief of staff at The Los Angeles Times, she reported to the executive editor and was a resource for the entire newsroom as it shaped new initiatives and strategic plans. That work included launching and expanding franchises like De Los, the 101 and Boiling Point. She also ran annual budgeting and goal-setting processes. Before that, she led the newsroom’s push to understand its audience, engage with data and find a path to sustainable subscription growth.


Earlier in her career, Alexa held insight and strategy roles at The Atlantic and The Correspondent. Most recently, she led strategic partnerships with educational content providers at Guild, an education and skilling platform. She studied history at Dartmouth and completed the Sulzberger Executive Leadership Program at the Columbia Journalism School.


She’ll be a partner to me and our leadership team as we build out the next chapter of Opinion, from video to talent.


Alexa is a Colorado native and an Angeleno of nearly a decade. She’s now relocating to New York, so send her your best taco and cinema recommendations.


Photo Credit: Johanna Matt-Navarro


Please join me in welcoming Jasmine and Alexa!


— Kathleen
